index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents an architectural overview of the proposed DHGAT model for heterogeneous graph representation learning. The global layout is structured as a horizontal pipeline from left to right, starting with an input heterogeneous graph HG(V,E,R), depicted as a small graph with five blue circular nodes connected by solid and dashed lines representing different edge types. This graph feeds into a large light-blue rectangular block labeled 'DHGAT(Φ,Ψ)', which serves as the core processing module. Below this main block, a detailed breakdown of DHGAT’s internal structure is shown within a teal-bordered rectangle, illustrating its two-stage composition: a Decision Net (Φ) followed by a Representation Net (Ψ). The output of DHGAT is passed through a yellow trapezoidal block labeled 'MLP' (Multilayer Perceptron), which produces the final prediction ŷ, represented as a vertical stack of six shaded rectangles indicating class probabilities or scores.

Within the DHGAT module, the Decision Net (Φ), shown as a medium-blue rectangle, processes each node and generates a probability vector ρ_v^l ∈ ℝ^|Γ| for each node v ∈ V at layer l. This is visualized as a stack of four light-blue rectangles. These probability vectors are then fed into a diamond-shaped node labeled 'G.s', which corresponds to the Gumbel-Softmax estimator, as indicated by the legend below the diagram. The output of Gumbel-Softmax is a discrete neighborhood type γ_v^l ∈ Γ for each node, represented as a stack of four smaller light-blue rectangles. This discrete selection is then passed to the Representation Net (Ψ), depicted as a light-green rectangle, which updates the node embeddings based on the chosen neighborhood type. The resulting node representations h_v^l ∈ ℝ^{d_l} are shown as a stack of four light-green rectangles.

Connections between modules are indicated by black arrows. The input graph HG(V,E,R) connects directly to the DHGAT block. Inside DHGAT, arrows flow sequentially from Decision Net (Φ) to the probability stack, then to Gumbel-Softmax, then to the discrete type stack, and finally to Representation Net (Ψ), which outputs the embedding stack. A large downward-pointing light-blue arrow from the DHGAT block visually emphasizes that it encapsulates the detailed inner workings shown below. The output of the embedding stack from Representation Net (Ψ) is implicitly fed into the MLP block via the top-level DHGAT output. The MLP block then produces the final prediction ŷ. All text labels are in black sans-serif font, with mathematical notations placed beneath corresponding components to denote their formal definitions.
